articles.headline: Celtics to extend guard Payton Pritchard on 2-year, $44.2M deal
articles.description: Celtics guard Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with a mutual option for the 2029-30 season.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics guard Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension, plus a mutual option in the 2029-30 season, CAA co-head of basketball Austin Brown and agent Max Saidman told ESPN on Tuesday.

Pritchard -- the 2024 NBA champion and 2025 Sixth Man of the Year -- cashes in on a fully guaranteed two-year max extension to keep him a key long-term member of the retooled Celtics after the 6-foot-1 guard averaged career highs in points (17), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season.

 

The deal keeps Pritchard for an additional season after his current deal ends in 2028. Pritchard will be set to make over $21 million for the 2028-29 season before a mutual option in 2029-30 worth $23 million. That mutual option allows either side to opt in for the final season of Pritchard's contract in 2029-30, which also opens the window for extension conversations that summer.

Pritchard blossomed last season while starting 50 games, helping to ease the loss of Jayson Tatum for most of last season by taking an increased role in the offense. His touches per game went from 51.8 in 2024-25 to nearly 70 last season, the second-largest increase among the 33 players to record at least 4,000 touches in each season.

Pritchard, 28, is one of four players to make at least 200 3-pointers in multiple seasons in Celtics history, along with Tatum, Derrick White and Antoine Walker. He has also been incredibly durable in his six NBA seasons; his 241 games played over the last three years is tied for the third-most in the league during that span.

The deal takes Pritchard, the No. 26 pick for the Celtics in the 2020 NBA draft, through at least his ninth season in Boston, and potentially Year 10 if the option is picked up.

articles.description: The NFL has issued a two-game suspension to Bears defensive end Montez Sweat for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances.
articles.body:
The NFL has issued a two-game suspension without pay to Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances.

Sweat will miss games this Sunday at the Atlanta Falcons and next Thursday night against the New England Patriots.

Sweat, in his fourth season with the Bears, has two sacks and four quarterback hits in five games this season.

He led the Bears with 10 sacks last season.

articles.headline: Eagles pass rusher Jalyx Hunt (leg) unlikely vs. Panthers
articles.description: Eagles pass rusher Jalyx Hunt, who sustained ankle and knee injuries last week, is not expected to play Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, DC Vic Fangio said.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- It would be "pretty miraculous" for Eagles edge rusher Jalyx Hunt to play Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said.

Hunt sustained ankle and knee injuries on the final play of the first half against the Jacksonville Jaguars last week. His left leg got pinned under him and twisted awkwardly as he attempted to recover a loose ball following a fourth-down stop from teammate Zack Baun. Hunt stayed on the ground for some time before exiting with the assistance of trainers.

"He's the kind of guy, he's going to be pushing the envelope and making the medical people clear him," Fangio said. "He's not going to be one of those guys that's going to be hesitant to come back."

Fellow edge rusher Jonathan Greenard was not able to suit up against the Jaguars after testing his injured ankle pregame. Fangio said "hopefully he'll be able to go this week" when asked about Greenard's status for the Panthers game.

The Eagles could be getting reinforcements on offense with receiver DeVonta Smith and running back Saquon Barkley on the mend from hamstring injuries.

"I'm hopeful," coach Nick Sirianni said Monday. "I just think it's hard to tell you one thing and then it plays out differently because there's still a lot of time left for this game. But I'm hopeful that these -- I know how hard these guys work to get themselves back because it's killing them that they're not out there."

The running back room in particular could use a boost with Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve and Will Shipley expected to miss multiple weeks after suffering a partial plantar fascia tear during the Jaguars game, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The safety position is another to keep an eye on. Marcus Epps missed the Jacksonville game with a groin injury, and Michael Carter II exited Sunday with an abdominal injury and did not return.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the biggest offseason signings, including Payton Pritchard's two-year extension with the Celtics.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason still features plenty of important moves across the league.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Oct. 13: Pritchard lands two-year extension

Payton Pritchard terms: Two years, $44.2 million

Grade: A

This deal is an easy grade for Boston, as Pritchard's production makes him worth considerably more. The 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year averaged a career-high 17.0 points and 5.2 assists per game last season, is a career 39% 3-point shooter and he's scored with above-average efficiency in five of his six NBA campaigns.

Yet because Pritchard is currently playing on such a team-friendly contract -- $30 million over four years -- he was limited to a $22.1 million annual salary for his next extension. There was also the possibility that Pritchard could decline to sign a new below-market contract and test free agency in 2028, but he will now be guaranteed more than double his career earnings without the risk of anything going awry over the next two years.

This extension carries little downside for Boston. Perhaps Pritchard will start to decline on his new deal, as he'll be a 30-year-old small guard by the time it begins, but he's far more likely to outplay it with the value he provides the Celtics.

Marks: NBA extension decisions to watch this week

Oct. 10: Warriors sign Podziemski to five-year extension

Brandin Podziemski terms: Five years, $110 million

Grade: B-

As I wrote recently when explaining why Podziemski is a candidate to make ESPN's NBA Rank top 100 next season, the Warriors guard is underrated because he's a jack of all trades, master of none. Podziemski is a good shooter, a good passer and a good defender, but he's not amazing at any of those skills, which means he profiles more as a quality role player than a long-term star.

An average annual salary of $22 million is a reasonable deal for that level of player, especially one in his early 20s. And the advanced metrics like Podziemski even more than his surface stats or reputation suggest.

This deal also fits into the Warriors' plans for next summer. According to ESPN's Anthony Slater, Podziemski's new deal will start at $18.9 million in the first year before increasing in subsequent seasons. Given that Podziemski would have had a cap hold of $17 million if he hadn't signed an extension, this extension will shave less than $2 million off the Warriors' cap space next offseason.

articles.body:
Tristan H. Cockcroft's 2026 fantasy football Knockout league rankings will be updated throughout the season to reflect the latest news, trends and opinions. Use them to inform your own rankings, or as a guide to draft your team. Sign up for your team for free.

Knockout leagues are our newest offering for 2026, challenging fantasy football managers to avoid being the last-place scorer in any given week, with the final team standing winning the championship. For those new to the format, here's a strategy primer to help you fine-tune your game.

The rankings below will differ slightly from our standard offering in that Knockout leagues begin with 18 teams, creating more demand at thinner positions such as quarterback and tight end. Additionally, week-over-week consistency carries additional weight, players with injury or other availability concerns are less desirable, and later-year bye weeks can prove advantageous. A standard 18-team knockout league comprises 14 slots including a kicker and a defense, so the rankings began 252 deep at season's start, and are now 182 deep (13 teams times 14 players) for leagues drafting to begin in Week 6, to take you from the first overall selection through to the final pick of the draft.

Remember that if you want to start a league that plays this week your draft must be completed by the time players lock for Thursday Night Football, otherwise your league will begin play the following week.  A 13-team league lets you eliminate 12 players through Week 17, leaving only the winner standing.

articles.body:
The NBA season starts in one week, but that isn't the only thing on the minds of league executives. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday, a day before the 2026-27 regular season tips off. 

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. That's currently far below the average of 11 rookie extensions signed per year since 2023, but expect that number to rise in the coming days. Of the 34 players to land rookie extensions in the past three seasons, 17 signed on deadline day.

What deals will the next week bring? We broke down what to expect for six of the 16 eligible players.

Rookie extension decisions aren't the only things we're watching. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans with two years remaining on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the deadline to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts.

Let's examine the league's most important extension decisions and what Monday's deadline could bring for teams around the league.

Jump to a section:

Six big rookie extension decisions

KAT, Giannis among vets to watch

Moves coming for Lakers, Knicks?

Rookie extension candidates to watch

Brandon Miller, Charlotte Hornets

Why an extension could get done: Following offseason trades of LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, the Hornets view Miller and Kon Knueppel as the franchise's new foundation. An injury-plagued sophomore 2024-25 season limited Miller to 27 games, but he rebounded last season to post career highs in 3-pointers made, 3-point percentage and free throw attempts and averaged more than 20 points per game for the second straight season.

 

Why it might not: Miller views Amen Thompson's five-year, $208 million extension with Houston as a comparable salary. The main difference: Thompson played at least 60 games in each of his first three seasons and was selected for the All-Defensive First Team in 2025.

What I would offer: Five years, $175 million. The contract can either start at $30.2 million and increase each year, ending at $39.8 million, or start high and decline each season. (Coby White's latest contract with the Hornets declines in Years 2 and 3.) With no player earning more than $25 million in 2027-28, Charlotte has the flexibility to increase Miller's offer. Not including new contracts for Miller and center Moussa Diabate, who is eligible for an extension in February, Charlotte projects to be $80 million under the luxury tax next season.

Dereck Lively II, Dallas Mavericks

Why an extension could get done: The Mavericks would need to bypass injury concerns and look at his impact when healthy. Despite playing only 36 games in 2024-25, Lively ranked 17th out of 138 players in offensive rebounding percentage and fourth in defensive rebounding percentage. articles.headline: Yes, it's OK to drop these underperformers from your fantasy football team
articles.description: You don't have to hold on to Justin Herbert, Kenny Gainwell, Coutland Sutton or other fantasy underperformers.
articles.body:
Perhaps you are aware that ESPN Fantasy delivers a rather extensive look at the top free agent players to add to your myriad football teams each and every Monday. I don't know the goofy fellow who writes it, but rumor is he looks quite like this. Regardless, the column analyzes players that tend to be in higher demand than the week prior, are available in at least 50% of ESPN leagues and are generally wise additions to your teams.

What that free agent column does not do is share the top options a fantasy manager, either on a winning or losing team, should send packing to free agency. So let's do that now.

Look, folks, it's October. Five weeks of the fantasy regular season are in the books, and so much has changed since draft day. Many things change every week, but we are seeing a whole lot of players on fantasy rosters who perhaps do not need to be there. We focus on ESPN standard leagues, because when the rules are different (roster sizes, roster spots, player scoring, etc.) then value is different. You're not dumping any starting QB in a superflex league, for example, not even the ones we name below.

Bottom line, what you really want to know, with all these players: "Is it OK to drop this guy, whom I so dearly coveted on draft day, but now truly hate to have on my roster?" With these guys, with the league-specific caveat above, you have our permission to move on.

 Justin Herbert, QB, Los Angeles Chargers (60.3% rostered)

What we believed six weeks ago: Herbert threw for 3,727 yards and 26 touchdowns last season, and only nine quarterbacks scored more fantasy points. This is a talented player, perhaps on a Hall of Fame track if he gets some future playoff luck, who once exceeded 50 touchdown passes in 2021. The Chargers hired generally acknowledged offensive genius Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator. The consensus was clear: Herbert might deliver his best season yet, and he became everyone's sleeper. What could possibly go wrong?

What we believe now: Herbert enters Week 6 averaging 10.7 fantasy points per game, well down from last season when it was 17.9 points. We thought, when Herbert scored only 13.26 points in a stunning loss to the hapless Arizona Cardinals in Week 1, that it was aberrant. It has been Herbert's top scoring output. The Chargers are winless! Blame McDaniel's new scheme, offensive line and WR injuries, a poor running game or whatever you like, but Herbert has been, arguably, the worst fantasy QB this season, and clearly so when considering he was the 10th quarterback off the board on draft day. The schedule eases up eventually but still, this isn't good.
Other quarterbacks to dump: Jaxson Dart, New York Giants (29.8%, injured, out for the season); Daniel Jones, Indianapolis Colts (18.8%); Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (8.7%); Cam Ward, Tennessee Titans (5.5%).

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: The rookies you should be targeting in drafts
articles.description: André Snellings looks at the rookie class and highlights which players to target in fantasy drafts this season.
articles.body:
The 2026 NBA draft class is special. It's one that we have been anticipating with high expectations for quite a while, and early indications are that this class will live up to those lofty expectations.

That translates to fantasy hoops as well. In a typical season, there are a small number of rookies discussed for fantasy drafts, but this season there are six currently with Average Draft Positions (ADPs) in the top 130 (meaning they are being picked in typical fantasy drafts). In addition, there are several others on the fringe that are either being drafted in deeper leagues or that will be on the radar as free agents of interest as soon as the season begins.

Let's take a closer look at the rookie class as the season approaches and discuss when you should consider taking them in your fantasy drafts.

Middle-round prospects

Caleb Wilson (ADP 75.2), Cameron Boozer (ADP 75.3) and AJ Dybantsa (ADP 76.1) are coming off fantasy draft boards in a similar range, around the seventh round. All three seem poised to start for their respective teams and contribute significantly out the gate.

 AJ Dybantsa, F, Washington Wizards: Dybantsa was the top overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft and was the leading scorer in college basketball as a freshman last season. He continued his scoring ways at the Las Vegas Summer League, averaging 25.0 PPG and 7.0 RPG in two games. He has started the first two preseason games for the Wizards and played a total of 46 minutes, notching an impressive combined stat line of 25 points, nine rebounds, five steals and four assists. Dybantsa is a strong candidate to lead the rookie class in scoring this season. He is good at drawing free throws and shoots a good percentage, but it should be noted that Dybantsa doesn't hit many 3-pointers for a volume scorer, and he may not have (m)any strong fantasy categories outside of scoring. Overall, Dybantsa is worthy of fantasy draft consideration in the middle rounds, but I have him ranked slightly lower than his ADP -- more top 85 than top 75 -- in both points and category leagues.

 Cameron Boozer, PF, Memphis Grizzlies: The third overall pick in the NBA draft has been the betting favorite to win NBA Rookie of the Year since draft night and sits at +300 to win at DraftKings. He was a 20-10 big man in college, but he is also a strong passer who scores efficiently and can knock down the 3-pointer. In his first three NBA preseason games, Boozer scored double-figures and produced strong per-minute rebound and assist totals in all three outings. The Grizzlies traded former franchise player Ja Morant this offseason, opening the way for Boozer to be the centerpiece of their rebuilding efforts. Boozer currently ranks top 70 in points leagues and top 80 in categories, just above his ADP in points leagues and right on his ADP in categories.

articles.headline: Real Madrid's Mourinho on media snub post-Villarreal: 'Watch first minute of game'
articles.description: José Mourinho has refused to explain why he skipped his post-match news conference after Real Madrid's 1-0 win over Villarreal,
articles.body:
José Mourinho has refused to explain why he skipped his post-match news conference after Real Madrid's 1-0 win over Villarreal, telling journalists to "watch the first minute of the game" to understand his decision.

Despite taking all three points in Saturday's LaLiga game, Madrid left the Bernabéu angry after Vinícius Júnior had a goal disallowed for a hair-pull -- for which he was then sent off -- in a dramatic passage of play in the second half.

Coach Mourinho then refused to speak to the media after the game, meaning Tuesday's news conference ahead of Madrid's Champions League clash with Roma was their first chance to question Mourinho on his motives.

"Nothing, nothing," Mourinho said, speaking at Roma's Olympic Stadium, when asked what he had to say about the incident. "This is a Champions League game. [I have] nothing to say about the league game."

"I told your colleague I didn't want to comment, but I'll try to make sure this is the last [question]," Mourinho said, when pressed on the subject. "I'd invite you just watch the first minute of the game against Villarreal. If you want, we can talk about it on Saturday [in his next news conference]. The first minute is enough, if you know."

Mourinho has criticised a number of refereeing performances and key decisions since his return to Madrid this summer.

After last month's Madrid derby, he brought a printout with photos of two key incidents which went against his team into his post-match news conference, saying the referee "couldn't cope with the pressure" and adding "congratulations to [refereeing committee] the CTA."

"I trust in all of them," Mourinho insisted on Tuesday, when asked if he trusted Champions League referees more than Spanish officials.

"The only thing that smells funny to me is when everyone knows the name of a referee three weeks before [a game], when it should be 24 hours. That's the only thing that makes me uncomfortable. Apart from that I have faith. I don't have any negative feelings."

Wedneday's game in Rome marks a return for Mourinho to a club where he spent three seasons, winning the 2022 Conference League.

articles.headlineJa: リヴァプールのイサク、ガクポ、ソボスライがLASKとのチャンピオンズリーグ戦を欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールは、水曜日に開催されるUEFAチャンピオンズリーグのLASK戦に、アレクサンダー・イサク、コディ・ガクポ、ドミニク・ソボスライの3名を欠場させる見通しです。
articles.body:
Liverpool are set to be without Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai for Wednesday's UEFA Champions League clash with LASK.

All three players missed the Reds' 3-0 defeat to Manchester City on Sunday after sustaining injuries during the international break. Isak and Gakpo both had to withdraw from international duty with a thigh injury and an ankle injury respectively while Szoboszlai returned from the Hungary camp with a tight hamstring.

The trio have all failed to recover in time for Wednesday's clash at Raiffeisen Arena and are not part of Liverpool's 23-player travelling party to Austria.

Speaking about Szoboszlai's fitness at the weekend, Iraola said: "Dom came from the national team with tightness, an overload. We put him as a floater in the training and tried to protect him but he was feeling something very small. It's true that now we play four games in 10 days, so it's going to be difficult because we fly to Austria in two days. I think it's going to be difficult to recover any of the players."

The Liverpool boss is expected to give a further update on the players' fitness in his prematch news conference on Tuesday.

articles.descriptionJa: バルセロナとレアル・マドリードが引き続きアーリング・ハーランドをマークする一方、チェルシーはボーンマスのアレックス・スコット獲得に自信を深めています。「トランスファー・トーク」が最新情報を伝えます。
articles.body:
Barcelona and Real Madrid were at Anfield on Sunday to watch Erling Haaland when Manchester City faced Liverpool. Meanwhile, Chelsea are growing confident they will be able to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott in January.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Barcelona and Real Madrid scouts were at Anfield to scout Manchester City striker Erling Haaland as he opened the scoring in a 3-0 win over Liverpool, according to TEAMtalk. Both of the Spanish giants continue to monitor the possibility of a future move following the club's guilty verdict for hundreds of financial charges. The two clubs weren't just there to watch City players, though: Barça have also been monitoring the situation of defender Ronald Araújo, who is on loan at Liverpool, while Madrid have been checking on Liverpool midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz.

- Chelsea are increasingly confident that they will sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott during the January transfer window, according to TEAMtalk. The belief is that the 23-year-old would find it difficult to turn down a move to Stamford Bridge and the Blues are willing to meet the Cherries' demands, with any deal likely to reach around £100 million. Bournemouth turned down all interest in Scott during the summer, but the England international's contract expires in 2028 and he has so far resisted any calls for an extension.

- Borussia Dortmund have been interested in U.S. youth international and Philadelphia Union striker Malik Jakupovic for some time, reports Sky Germany. In the summer, the Bundesliga club submitted an offer for the 17-year-old that was worth €2m-€3m but was ultimately rejected. Contact continues to exist but there is major competition for Jakupovic with Chelsea, RB Salzburg and Stuttgart all looking at him while Eintracht Frankfurt also have in the past.

- Chelsea will need at least £50 million to tempt Barcelona into letting midfielder Frenkie de Jong leave in the January transfer window, according to Football Insider. Chelsea are looking at the 29-year-old as they continue their efforts to replace Enzo Fernández after the Argentina international joined Manchester City in the summer. De Jong is out injured but the Dutch midfield is nearing a return to fitness, although that return could make a move more difficult for the Blues as Barça have been eagerly awaiting his return.

- Ruben Amorim wants AC Milan to sign Sassuolo midfielder Darryl Bakola, who has also received interest from Roma and Juventus, reports Calciomercato. Amorim was surprised by the 18-year-old's quality when the Rossoneri drew 1-1 against Sassuolo at Mapei Stadium, when Bakola was named man of the match. The young Frenchman is being considered by scouts across Europe, and having been signed for €10 million plus €2 million in add-ons last January, he could now command over €30 million.
